summary: Las 4 Estrellas: Asteroid Dodge is an arcade-style Scratch video game created by elementary school students for the Space Video Game challenge. Players control an astronaut at the bottom of the screen who must dodge asteroids falling vertically from space—earning 1 point for every asteroid avoided and managing 3 lives before hitting Game Over—inspired by NASA's astronaut safety and space debris tracking efforts.
details:
What It Does:

Las 4 Estrellas: Asteroid Dodge is an interactive video game built in Scratch where players guide an astronaut across the bottom of the screen to survive a vertical asteroid shower. Every asteroid that safely passes without touching the astronaut awards +1 point. The player starts with 3 lives, losing 1 life each time an asteroid hits the astronaut until all 3 lives are gone and the game ends in a Game Over screen.

How It Works & How We Built It:

Our elementary school team (grades 2–4) designed and programmed the entire game in Scratch. We coded horizontal player movement, continuous vertical falling trajectories for the asteroids, collision detection between sprites, and two real-time game variables: a Score counter (+1 per dodged asteroid) and a Lives counter (starting at 3 and decreasing upon impact).

Why It Matters:

Space debris and micrometeoroids are real hazards that astronauts and spacecraft face in orbit. Inspired by NASA's spacewalk safety protocols and Near-Earth Object tracking, our game introduces young learners to space hazard awareness through an intuitive, engaging challenge that builds reflexes and problem-solving skills.

Tools & Resources Used:

- Scratch (MIT) for game programming, variable tracking (score and lives), and collision logic

- Custom astronaut and asteroid sprites with space backgrounds

- Inspiration from NASA astronaut EVA safety and asteroid imagery
